{{Orphan|date=December 2024}}

In [[set theory]], an '''honest leftmost branch''' of a [[Tree (set theory)|tree]] ''T'' on ω&nbsp;×&nbsp;γ is a branch ([[maximal element|maximal]] [[Chain (order theory)|chain]]) ''ƒ'' ∈ [''T''] such that for each branch ''g'' ∈ [''T''], one has ∀ ''n'' ∈ ω : ''ƒ''(''n'')&nbsp;≤&nbsp;''g''(''n''). Here, [''T''] denotes the set of branches of maximal length of ''T'', ω is the smallest infinite [[ordinal number|ordinal]] (represented by the [[natural number]]s '''N'''), and γ is some other ordinal.
